subject: AI & Agents
title: AI in Criminal Justice
description: One-minute skill: AI in Criminal Justice.

hook.text: A judge uses an algorithm to decide bail. The defendant never learns what factors sealed their fate.

buildup.text: Risk assessment tools like COMPAS score defendants' likelihood of reoffending.

discovery.text: ProPublica found COMPAS wrongly labeled Black defendants as high-risk nearly twice as often.

twist.text: Northpointe (COMPAS maker) argued the tool was calibrated fairly — using a different definition of fair.

climax.text: Both sides were statistically correct. Different fairness metrics give different verdicts.

punchline.text: When freedom depends on an algorithm, the definition of fair matters most.

quiz.question: What controversy surrounds the COMPAS risk assessment tool?
options: It showed racial disparities in risk predictions
It was too expensive for courts

details.summary: AI tools help courts set bail, predict recidivism, and allocate policing resources. While promising efficiency, these systems risk encoding racial and socioeconomic biases into the justice system.
details.whyItMatters: Criminal justice decisions affect liberty and life. When AI influences these outcomes, ensuring fairness and due process becomes a fundamental rights issue.
takeaways: AI assists with bail, sentencing, and recidivism prediction
These tools can encode existing biases in the justice system
Due process requires transparency in algorithmic decision-making

faq.question: How is AI used in the criminal justice system?
faq.answer: Courts use risk assessment tools like COMPAS to predict recidivism. Police departments use predictive policing to allocate resources. AI also assists with evidence analysis and suspect identification.

faq.question: Is AI in criminal justice fair to all racial groups?
faq.answer: Studies show significant disparities. ProPublica found that COMPAS incorrectly flagged Black defendants as higher risk at nearly twice the rate of white defendants with similar profiles.
